business_scope.primary_industry_name: Publishing of PC and Console Video Games via Digital Stores

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: BVI Business Companies Act, 2004 (Cap. 218 of the Laws of the British Virgin Islands), ss. 9-19; Companies Act 2006 (UK), ss. 1043-1046; the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009 (SI 2009/1919), regs. 4-16, on registration of the BVI company as an overseas company in the United Kingdom.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission, Road Town, Tortola, British Virgin Islands; for UK establishment registration: Companies House, Cardiff CF14 3UZ, United Kingdom.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: BVI: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association with Certificate of Incorporation issued by the BVI Registrar; UK: Form OS01 - Application by an Overseas Company for Registration of a UK Establishment.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a BVI Business Company; no UK overseas-establishment capital requirement; shares may be issued as no-par-value ordinary shares and no escrow deposit or capital undertaking is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IT IS RESOLVED THAT the subscription for 10,000 no-par-value Ordinary Shares be approved, ratified, and the allotment to the subscriber be authorized. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the registered office be fixed at the BVI licensed registered agent's address, that the registered agent be appointed, and that the UK service address be adopted if required. IT IS FURTHER RESOLVED THAT [names of directors] be appointed as directors, [name] be appointed as corporate secretary, and such officers be authorized to make all formation filings with the BVI Registry and Companies House, to open payment-processor and EMI accounts, and to take all related actions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and preparation of BVI constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission, via a licensed BVI registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed BVI registered agent to submit the proposed company name, with an approved BVI corporate marker, for availability clearance. Prepare and execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association establishing no-par-value share authority, the BVI registered office, and the registered agent appointment.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name and approved marker
Certified passport copy of subscriber
Proof of residential address of subscriber
Consent to act as BVI registered agent
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, submit alternative names or apply to the Registrar for reconsideration under the BVI Business Companies Act; correct formal defects and resubmit promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: BVI incorporation filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registry of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission, through the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed constitutional documents and supporting consents with the Registry, calculate and pay the government incorporation fee, and request issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation. The certificate is issued once the Registrar is satisfied; the company comes into existence on the date entered in the Registry.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Registered agent and registered office consent forms
Government fee payment receipt
Certificate of Incorporation request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry rejects or returns the filing, correct the stated defect and refile within the Registry's response window; request administrative correction if the Certificate contains typographical or mapping errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First board resolution, share allotment and officer appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the BVI Business Company and the corporate secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the first board resolution approving the subscriber share subscription and the allotment of shares, confirming the BVI registered agent and registered office, and appointing directors, the corporate secretary, and any UK authorized representative. Maintain the required statutory registers and issue share certificates.
required_dossiers: Written resolution of the subscriber or incorporator
Consents to act of directors and secretary
Share register and register of directors
Draft share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank, processor, or regulator queries the corporate authorisations, pass a confirmatory board resolution and provide certified extracts of minutes and registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: UK overseas company registration with Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House, Crown Way, Cardiff CF14 3UZ, United Kingdom (WebFiling for overseas companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the BVI company will maintain a physical presence or place of business in the United Kingdom, file Form OS01 with Companies House within one month of opening the UK establishment. Attach certified copies of the BVI Certificate of Incorporation and constitutional documents, with an English translation if required, and appoint a UK person authorised to accept service. Companies House issues a UK establishment registration number after approval.
required_dossiers: Duly completed Form OS01
Certified copy of BVI Certificate of Incorporation
Certified copy of Memorandum and Articles of Association
Certified English translation if the originals are not in English
Particulars of directors, secretary, and UK authorised person
Consent to the UK registered office or service address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Companies House issues a query, file a corrected Form OS01 with supporting evidence within the stated correction period; if the one-month deadline was missed, file immediately and make a written mitigation request against any late filing penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance registers, AML/KYB and payment-rail onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BVI registered agent, board of directors, and Steam Valve Payout and PlayStation Store Payout partner onboarding desks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the statutory corporate governance records including registers of members, directors, secretary, and charges, and the BVI beneficial ownership register. Submit the required certified documentation to Steam and PlayStation partner onboarding and to the chosen EMI or bank to satisfy KYB checks for USD or EUR payout routing. This step does not require a statutory operating licence for digital video-game publishing.
required_dossiers: Register of members, directors and charges
BVI beneficial ownership register records
Certificate of Good Standing
Certified incorporation documents for KYB
Payment-rail and EMI onboarding forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KYB or partner onboarding is rejected, provide updated certified good standing evidence, a board resolution confirming authorised signatories, and a concise explanation of the company's economic substance and tax-exempt status.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - digital software publishing under ISIC 5820 is not an industrial or manufacturing activity requiring an industrial operating licence in the United Kingdom or British Virgin Islands.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Nil - no operating licence, manufacturing permit, or trade-specific regulatory permit is required for PC and console game publishing through Steam and PlayStation Store.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not applicable; if a physical UK office is occupied, the Environment Agency in England and Wales, the Scottish Environment Protection Agency in Scotland, or the Northern Ireland Environment Agency may regulate consequential waste or emissions, but no EIA will be triggered for office-only operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no EIA screening or development consent order is required for software publishing; the activity does not fall within a scheduled EIA project category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital publishing. If physical premises are used, comply with Building Regulations Part L, the Water Industry Act 1991 for any trade effluent, and WEEE or electrical waste provisions only when placing physical media or hardware on the market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No civil-defence clearance is required. For any UK office, comply with the Regulatory Reform Fire Safety Order 2005 by completing a fire-risk assessment and maintaining fire safety arrangements; under the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and the Workplace Health, Safety and Welfare Regulations 1992, ensure adequate ventilation, lighting, electrical safety and general workplace welfare. No structural load inspection is mandated for standard office use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC); digital portal: HMRC Online Services (https://www.tax.service.gov.uk/) and Companies House for entity registration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity (including a BVI Business Company) with a UK VAT registration obligation must apply for a UK VAT number via form VAT1 (or VAT1G for groups/non-established taxable persons) through HMRC's Online Services. Before VAT registration, the foreign entity should obtain a UK Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) if it has UK source income or corporation tax liabilities; for VAT-only purposes, HMRC issues a separate VAT registration number. The application must provide entity constitutional documents, evidence of economic activity in the UK, UK establishment details (if any), and a UK or EEA address for correspondence unless an agent is appointed. HMRC must issue the VAT registration certificate within 30 days of a complete application, and the effective date of registration is generally the date when the taxable turnover threshold was exceeded or, for voluntary registration, the date requested.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (as to BVI BC's BVI-source income and passive worldwide income; however, UK-indirect-tax nexus applies separately based on UK VAT registration thresholds and the place-of-supply rules for digital services).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No UK general check-the-box election exists for foreign entities; a BVI BC may elect to be treated as a 'non-established taxable person' for UK VAT if it has no UK establishment, or may apply for VAT group registration under the Value Added Tax Act 1994, Schedule 1, if it has a UK establishment with a UK-established entity. Corporation Tax (if a PE arises in the UK) follows the OECD Model Tax Convention attribution rules and UK CTA 2010 Part 3; no hybrid mismatch election is available, but UK anti-hybrid rules (TIOPA 2010 Part 6A) may apply to instrument or entity mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GBP 90,000 (UK taxable turnover threshold for established businesses); for non-established overseas businesses, there is no threshold and registration is required from the first supply of UK taxable services/goods, subject to the place-of-supply rules for Business-to-Consumer digital services under the Overseas Business Scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or mandatory e-invoicing clearance regime (as of 2026); taxpayers may use standard VAT invoicing. HMRC operates Making Tax Digital (MTD) for VAT requiring digital record-keeping and submission of VAT returns via functional compatible software (API-based) for VAT-registered businesses with taxable turnover above GBP 10,000, with mandatory MTD for all VAT-registered businesses from April 2022. There is no digital stamping; MTD APIs (HMRC VAT API v1.0) transmit nine-box VAT return data to HMRC with a 'declaration' timestamp; invoice stamping is not required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: UK VAT zero-rating applies to exports of goods if (1) the exporter retains evidence of export within specified time limits (usually 3 months from the time of supply; extended cases allowed), (2) the goods are supplied to a customer outside the UK and are exported from the UK, and (3) the supplier obtains and preserves 'valid evidence of export' as required by VAT Notice 703 (e.g., shipping documents, customs entries, or authenticated commercial documents). For digital services (including game sales via Steam/PlayStation online stores), exports of electronically supplied services to non-UK recipients are generally 'outside the scope' of UK VAT rather than zero-rated if the place of supply is outside the UK; for B2C supplies of digital services to UK consumers, the UK place of supply rule applies and UK VAT is chargeable at 20%, with the overseas seller using the VAT Mini One Stop Shop (MOSS) or UK non-established taxable person registration. Offshore supplies of digital games to non-UK consumers do not enjoy a refund mechanism because no UK VAT is chargeable; input VAT recovery is available under the 13th Directive procedure for non-established businesses only if the supplies are taxable UK supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / CHIEF declaration or CDS export entry)
Bill of Lading or airway bill / consignment note
Proof of export (carrier's certificate, shipping note, or HM Revenue & Customs export receipt)
Inward Remittance Certificate (only where separately required by banking or anti-money-laundering controls; not a statutory VAT evidence requirement)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: HMRC may deny zero-rating and assess VAT at 20% plus interest if the exporter fails to obtain valid evidence of export within the prescribed period. Penalties include: (i) a VAT evasion civil penalty of up to 100% of the VAT evaded for dishonest conduct (Finance Act 2007, Schedule 24), (ii) failure-to-notify penalties of up to 100% of the tax (for deliberate non-notification), (iii) accuracy penalties up to 100% for careless/deliberate inaccuracies (Schedule 24 FA 2007), (iv) late submission penalties GBP 5-15 per day under the default surcharge regime (replaced by points-based late payment regime), and (v) criminal prosecution under the VAT Act 1994 Section 72 and the Fraud Act 2006 for fraudulent evasion, carrying imprisonment up to 7 years and unlimited fines. HMRC has retrospective assessment powers of up to 20 years for deliberate non-disclosure (TMA 1970, Schedule 1A), and may issue assessments for four years for ordinary carelessness or six years for careless errors. Subject to the rights of third-party ownership, HMRC may also issue a joint and several liability notice to directors or shadow directors under Finance Act 2007, Schedule 24, paragraph 17C.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (Prudential Regulation Authority) in conjunction with HM Treasury (macro-financial policy) and the Financial Conduct Authority (bank conduct and AML supervision); exchange-control and sanctions enforcement is administered by HM Treasury's Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom maintains full and unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital accounts under the IMF Article VIII obligations; there are no exchange controls, no requirement for HM Treasury approval on inbound equity injections, no restrictions on dividend/royalty/profit remittances, and no obligation to channel transactions through a licensed domestic bank, though banks apply standard OFSI sanctions screening and source-of-funds verification; the 1979 abolition of UK exchange controls plus the Code for Capital Movements under OECD liberalisation codes ensure free capital movement within OECD and EU (post-Brexit, a unilateral liberal regime remains)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory timeline, no minimum mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to surrender export proceeds into GBP; the BVI company may retain, bank, and settle 100% of Steam/PlayStation sales proceeds in USD or any freely convertible currency; for statistical purposes HMRC may record the BOP classification, but no haircut, conversion, or central bank settlement window applies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BVI Annual Return (s.101C of the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004, as amended by the Companies (Amendment) Act 2022)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Corporate Affairs, BVI Financial Services Commission (submitted by the licensed BVI registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the end of the company's financial year (anniversary-based rule; e.g., financial year ending 31 December → filing due by 30 September of the following calendar year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of US$250 per annual return, plus a summary-conviction fine of up to US$5,000; continued default after Registrar notice is a ground for administrative strike-off, followed by restoration costs and reinstatement procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual BVI Economic Substance Return (ESR) under the Economic Substance (Companies and Limited Partnerships) Act, 2018 — relevant-activity declaration for the Steam/console publishing model
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: International Tax Authority of the BVI (filed electronically through the registered agent's portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the financial year end (same anniversary cycle as the Annual Return; e.g., FYE 31 December → ESR due by 30 September of the following year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing penalty of up to US$20,000 per return; failure to meet the economic substance test following ITA notice attracts escalating fines (up to US$250,000) and imprisonment up to 5 years for directors; findings may be exchanged with HMRC under the UK-BVI information exchange framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Secure Search System (BOSS) annual UBO confirmation statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BVI Financial Services Commission (confidential BOSS database; filed by the registered agent, not public)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every 12 months on the registered agent's compliance calendar (no fixed government date); any share transfer or UBO change must be filed within 15 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: AML/CFT sanctions apply to the company and the registered agent, including civil fines of up to US$500,000 for defective BO filing and criminal liability for knowingly false declarations; persistent default impairs the company's certificate of good standing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-, asset-, or employee-based audit threshold applies to a private BVI Business Company. A statutory audit becomes compulsory only where the company is listed on a recognized exchange, holds a BVI FSC-regulated licence, or the International Tax Authority requires audited accounts to verify economic substance compliance (relevant for IP-business filings). The Steam/console publishing entity therefore remains audit-exempt at the BVI statutory level unless such a trigger arises.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is the default statutory standard under s.67 of the BVI Business Companies Act, 2004; financial records must be sufficient to prepare fair-view IFRS financial statements. For consolidation inside the GB (UK) group, the parent reporting pack must be prepared on an IFRS basis (or reconciled from US GAAP/UK GAAP), and the BVI records must be retained for a minimum of 5 years under BVI law; a 7-year retention policy is applied to satisfy UK group audit, transfer-pricing, and CFC documentation requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The BVI registered agent acts as the AML officer for the company and must positively confirm, at least once every 12 months, that the BOSS filing and the in-office UBO register (Register of Members) remain accurate and complete; the annual confirmation is executed by circular resolution or compliance certificate issued to the directors. Any share transfer or change in the ownership chain must be notified in writing and a BOSS update submitted within 15 days of the change; a no-change confirmation is accepted at the annual review where no transfer occurred. The GB (UK) parent's PSC register must separately disclose the ultimate individual(s) controlling the BVI company where the group is subject to UK transparency rules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 – US$2,500 per annum (licensed BVI registered agent and registered office, including annual return preparation, statutory register upkeep, meeting minutes, and UBO/BOSS annual confirmation; higher substance-administration work for an IP-holding Steam publisher is billed at the upper end).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000 – US$9,000 per annum for a full IFRS audit of a private BVI publishing/IP holding company; typically nil in audit-exempt years where the entity instead prepares a compilation report and intercompany reporting pack for the UK parent.

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (main rate for FY 2023 onwards: profits above £250,000; 19% Small Profits Rate for profits below £50,000; marginal relief applies between £50,000 and £250,000)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No full tax holidays. Video Games Tax Relief (VGTR) provides an enhanced deduction for qualifying core expenditure on British-certified video games (currently up to 55% for qualifying expenditure) and is available on the central design/development element; R&D expenditure credit can reduce effective rate; taxable profits of a non-UK resident BVI company are limited to UK-source trading profits attributable to a UK permanent establishment.
